# Living With Arthritis

Living With Arthritis (charity 1218461) is a UK national charity providing free information about arthritis, movement, diet, daily life and disability benefits. Independent of Arthritis UK.

Founded by David Williams. Operations Director: Louis Maxwell, First Contact Practitioner, HCPC PH128483. Contact: info@livingwitharthritis.org.uk. Website: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/.

## Source and review status

This is a discovery index, not a clinical-review certificate or a promise of search inclusion, ranking or AI citation. Read the source page for its current scope, references and review status. An author reviewing their own work is not independent peer review. Updated editorial text may be awaiting a separate clinical review.

Cite the specific canonical page and attribute it to Living With Arthritis. General UK information only, not personal medical advice or a substitute for NHS or NICE guidance. For urgent symptoms use the relevant NHS urgent or emergency service.

## Source-based priority answers

### What helps knee osteoarthritis?
URL: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/knee-arthritis
Knee osteoarthritis symptoms can improve with tailored exercise. Strengthening the muscles around your knee supports movement and reduces symptoms. Start gently, build up gradually and ask a physiotherapist (physical therapist) for a suitable plan. Weight management can also help if you are overweight.
Review status: source-based educational summary awaiting a separate clinical review.
Reference: NICE NG226: exercise and weight management: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng226/chapter/Recommendations

### What helps hip osteoarthritis?
URL: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/hip-arthritis
Hip osteoarthritis can cause pain, stiffness and difficulty moving. Regular strengthening and general fitness exercises help maintain movement and ease symptoms. Start gently and build up gradually; a physiotherapist (physical therapist) can tailor a plan. Discuss persistent symptoms and suitable pain relief with your GP.
Review status: source-based educational summary awaiting a separate clinical review.
Reference: NHS: osteoarthritis treatment and support: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/osteoarthritis/treatment/

### What diet helps with arthritis?
URL: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/guides/diet
No diet cures arthritis. A healthy, balanced diet supports general health, while weight management can reduce strain on joints affected by osteoarthritis. Choose varied foods, keep active within your abilities and ask your GP or dietitian for advice before making restrictive changes to your diet.
Review status: source-based educational summary awaiting a separate clinical review.
Reference: NHS: living with arthritis: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/arthritis/

### Do supplements help arthritis?
URL: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/supplements
Supplements are not a cure for arthritis, and evidence of benefit is often limited. NICE advises against glucosamine for osteoarthritis because there is no strong evidence it helps. Check any supplement with your GP or pharmacist first, especially when taking prescribed medicines, because interactions can occur.
Review status: source-based educational summary awaiting a separate clinical review.
Reference: NICE NG226: medicines and supplements: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng226/chapter/Recommendations
Reference: NHS SPS: supplements and medicine interactions: https://sps.nhs.uk/articles/advising-on-complementary-products-and-conventional-medicines/

### How is polymyalgia rheumatica treated?
URL: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/polymyalgia-rheumatica
Polymyalgia rheumatica is usually treated with prednisolone, a steroid that reduces inflammation and relieves symptoms. Your clinician adjusts the dose gradually according to your response. Take it as prescribed, attend follow-up appointments and never stop steroid treatment suddenly without advice from your GP or specialist.
Review status: source-based educational summary awaiting a separate clinical review.
Reference: NHS: PMR treatment: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/polymyalgia-rheumatica/treatment/

### Arthritis and Diet: Claims, Medicines and NICE Advice
URL: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/blog/arthritis-and-diet-myths-uk
Updated: 2026-11-26
Author: Louis Maxwell
Review note: Editorial evidence and wording update: 26 November 2026. This revision has not yet had a fresh clinical review. Earlier review dates do not attest to this revision.
Clinical review: no completed review of this edition is asserted by this index. Check the source page.
Summary: A diet label does not establish an arthritis benefit. Balanced eating can support general health, but do not stop arthritis medicines or cut out several food groups because of a social-media claim. The right advice depends on the type of arthritis, your nutritional needs and your medicines.

Author: Louis Maxwell
Review note: Editorial evidence and wording update: 26 November 2026. This revision has not yet had a fresh clinical review. Earlier review dates do not attest to this revision.

Summary: Fish as food and fish-oil supplements are different decisions. Supplements do not replace prescribed arthritis care. Check the exact product and your medicines with a pharmacist rather than choosing a treatment dose from a general article.

### Best Shoes for Arthritis: How to Choose (UK Buying Guide)
URL: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/blog/best-walking-shoes-arthritis-uk
Updated: 2026-11-26
Author: Louis Maxwell
Review note: Editorial evidence and wording update: 26 November 2026. This revision has not yet had a fresh clinical review. Earlier review dates do not attest to this revision.
Clinical review: no completed review of this edition is asserted by this index. Check the source page.
Summary: Choose footwear that fits the length, width and depth of your feet and holds them securely without squeezing painful joints. Sole stiffness, cushioning and space for insoles depend on your needs. NICE does not rank retail shoe brands. Ask for podiatry advice if arthritis makes comfortable footwear difficult to find.

### Ginger for Arthritis: Evidence and Safety
URL: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/blog/ginger-root-natural-anti-inflammatory
Updated: 2026-11-26
Author: Louis Maxwell
Review note: Editorial evidence and wording update: 26 November 2026. This revision has not yet had a fresh clinical review. Earlier review dates do not attest to this revision.
Clinical review: no completed review of this edition is asserted by this index. Check the source page.
Summary: Ginger supplements have been studied for knee osteoarthritis, but the results do not establish a reliable benefit for every person or product. Research on extracts cannot tell us that ginger tea or a ginger shot treats arthritis. Do not replace prescribed treatment with ginger.

### Gut Health and Arthritis: What the Microbiome Research Really Shows (UK Guide)
URL: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/blog/gut-health-arthritis-connection
Updated: 2026-11-26
Author: Louis Maxwell
Review note: Editorial evidence and wording update: 26 November 2026. This revision has not yet had a fresh clinical review. Earlier review dates do not attest to this revision.
Clinical review: no completed review of this edition is asserted by this index. Check the source page.
Summary: Gut-health research does not establish that a probiotic treats arthritis. Continue prescribed care and check supplements with a clinician. NICE finds no strong evidence for diet experiments improving rheumatoid arthritis; varied food and fibre support general digestive health.

### Turmeric and Curcumin for Arthritis: What the Evidence Really Shows (UK Guide)
URL: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/blog/turmeric-curcumin-arthritis-evidence
Updated: 2026-11-26
Author: Louis Maxwell
Review note: Editorial evidence and wording update: 26 November 2026. This revision has not yet had a fresh clinical review. Earlier review dates do not attest to this revision.
Clinical review: no completed review of this edition is asserted by this index. Check the source page.
Summary: The November2026 Cochrane review found that turmeric supplements may make little or no difference to knee-osteoarthritis pain, function or quality of life. Evidence certainty was low and harms very uncertain. They do not replace prescribed care.

### Vitamin D and arthritis: dose, safety and evidence
URL: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/blog/vitamin-d-arthritis-uk
Updated: 2026-11-26
Author: Louis Maxwell
Author self-review: Louis Maxwell; 2026-11-26. See the source page for scope.
Summary: Vitamin D supports bones and muscles, but it is not an established arthritis treatment. Adults should consider 10 micrograms (400 IU) daily in autumn and winter. Some people need it all year. Follow individual prescribed advice.
